item.title: Oyo 2027: I won’t step down for anyone, ADC guber candidate vows
item.description: By Adeola Badru The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adegboyega Adegoke, has dismissed rumours that he is planning to withdraw from the 2027 governorship race, declaring that he is determined to contest and win the election. Adegoke, who described himself as a committed contender in the race, said he would not step down for any candidate under any circumstances, insisting that his ambition was driven by his determination to implement his policy agenda, tagged SOLUTIONS, for the benefit of residents of the state. The ADC candidate made his position known in a statement issued by his media team on Tuesday, in which he described the reports of his planned withdrawal as unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. He said he remained resolute in his ambition to become the next governor of Oyo State, adding that he was not in the race as a placeholder for any other candidate. “Let me state unequivocally that I am not stepping down for anybody. I am in this race to win and become the next occupier of the Agodi Governor’s Office,” Adegoke said. He added: “The rumour is unfounded, unfortunate and misleading. I have stated many times that I am not a placeholder. I am the Oyo State governorship candidate of our great party, the African Democratic Congress (ADC), the next Executive Governor of Oyo State, Insha Allah.” Adegoke said his ambition was anchored on his determination to deliver the promises contained in his SOLUTIONS agenda, which he said was designed to address the needs of the people and improve their welfare. He urged his supporters across the state to remain steadfast and not allow the rumours to distract them from the campaign, assuring them that he remained fully committed to the governorship contest. The ADC candidate attributed the speculation to individuals who, according to him, were unsettled by his growing popularity and prospects of victory at the polls. He further expressed confidence that his ambition would be realised, declaring that no individual or group could frustrate what he described as God’s plan for his emergence as the next governor of Oyo State. “Nobody can stop the plan of God to make me the next Executive Governor of Oyo State,” he said. item.title: Northern governors dissolve NNDC board, order reorganisation
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA — The 19 Northern States, which jointly own the New Nigerian Development Company (NNDC), have resolved to dissolve its Board of Directors and constitute a new one as part of efforts to reposition the company. The decision was taken by the Secretaries to the Governments of the 19 Northern States, representing their respective state governments as shareholders, at a Special General Meeting held in Kaduna on Tuesday. However, the dissolution will take effect upon the valid adoption of the relevant ordinary resolutions at a duly convened General Meeting and compliance with applicable statutory requirements. Addressing journalists after the meeting, the Secretary to the Gombe State Government, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, said the shareholders had resolved to undertake a comprehensive reorganisation and repositioning of the company. He said the exercise was aimed at strengthening NNDC’s institutional capacity, improving corporate governance, enhancing operational efficiency and repositioning it as a viable investment and development institution serving the collective economic interests of the 19 Northern States. Njodi disclosed that a new Board of Directors would be constituted to provide strategic leadership, effective supervision, policy direction and corporate oversight. He said the composition, nomination and appointment of the new board would reflect the ownership interests of the participating states, the provisions of the company’s Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the requirements of the Companies and Allied Matters Act (CAMA) 2020. According to him, shareholders would subsequently approve the nominations and appointments of the new directors in accordance with the company’s constitutional documents and applicable laws. The Gombe SSG said the incoming board, upon its lawful constitution, had been directed to undertake a comprehensive review of the company’s existing management structure, personnel, administrative arrangements, operational framework and performance. He added that the new board would take appropriate measures to reorganise and strengthen the company’s management to promote accountability, professionalism and improved corporate performance, in line with its statutory and fiduciary responsibilities and applicable employment laws. Njodi further disclosed that the incoming board would conduct a comprehensive corporate governance, financial, administrative and operational audit of the company. He said the audit would examine NNDC’s financial position, assets and liabilities, existing investments, subsidiaries, joint ventures and commercial interests. It would also assess the performance and profitability of the company’s investments, compliance with statutory, regulatory and corporate governance obligations, as well as existing contractual commitments and outstanding obligations. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.description: … INEC raises concern over electoral law violations; Disu warns politicians against sponsoring thugs By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has raised concerns over violations of electoral laws by political actors ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning political parties to comply strictly with regulations governing campaigns, rallies and other electoral activities. Similarly, the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu, has warned politicians and political party leaders against sponsoring violence, recruiting thugs and deploying dangerous weapons to intimidate political opponents, declaring that the Nigeria Police Force would not tolerate electoral violence. They spoke on Tuesday at a high-level security meeting at the Force Headquarters, Abuja, attended by national chairmen, secretaries and executives of registered political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations and other stakeholders. He warned that when political actors could not freely assemble, organise campaigns or express their views without intimidation, the democratic process was already being undermined before election day. Amupitan said the commission considered it necessary to temporarily suspend its activities to participate in the meeting because of the seriousness of the security challenges confronting the country’s electoral process. “Political competition should not be turned into a battlefield,” he said, urging political parties to focus on presenting their manifestos, policies and ideas to Nigerians rather than engaging in violence. He stressed that strict compliance with electoral laws and procedures was essential as political activities intensified ahead of the next general election. The INEC chairman recalled his earlier engagement with political party leaders and members of the National Peace Committee on August 18, 2026, where he emphasised the need for peaceful political competition. He said the credibility of elections depended not only on the integrity of the voting process but also on the political environment in which campaigns and other activities were conducted. Amupitan noted that attacks on political party members and other citizens could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the electoral process. He urged political stakeholders to operate within the boundaries established by the Constitution and electoral laws, stressing that the security and welfare of Nigerians must remain a priority. item.title: ‘The truth is on the pitch’ – Senegal Football Federation hails CAS verdict
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) has welcomed the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling restoring Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the 2026 Africa Cup of Nations final, saying the decision has established the truth of the match on the pitch. The federation disclosed that it had received official notification of the CAS verdict, which upheld its appeal against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF). In its statement, the FSF said, “With this decision, the truth of the match is established on the pitch,” describing the ruling as a vindication of the result recorded during the final in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Senegal had beaten Morocco 1-0 after extra time to win the tournament. However, CAF’s Appeals Jury subsequently overturned the result and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory by forfeiture, prompting the Senegalese federation to appeal to CAS. The Senegalese federation expressed gratitude to the players, technical crew, team management, lawyers and advisers who worked on the case. It also thanked the country’s President and government, as well as supporters in Senegal and across the diaspora. FSF President, Abdoulaye Fall, described the ruling as a victory for fairness in sport and reaffirmed the federation’s commitment to maintaining cordial relations with Morocco. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has delivered justice to sport. I wish to strongly reaffirm the bonds of fraternity that unite us with the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) and the Moroccan people. “Senegalese football now resolutely looks to the future, with confidence and enthusiasm, in an Africa united around the values of sport,” Fall said. The final was marked by controversy after Senegalese players briefly left the pitch in protest against a penalty awarded to Morocco late in regulation time. The players later returned, but Morocco’s Brahim Diaz failed to convert the penalty. Senegal subsequently scored through Pape Gueye in extra time to secure the victory. Morocco challenged the result, and CAF’s Appeals Jury eventually ruled in its favour, declaring Senegal to have forfeited the match. Senegal then appealed to CAS, which overturned CAF’s decision and restored the original 1-0 result, confirming Senegal as champions of the 2026 AFCON. item.title: Hardship: Be patient with Tinubu, Akiolu urges Nigerians
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Oba of Lagos, Rilwan Akiolu, has urged Nigerians to exercise patience with President Bola Tinubu’s administration, expressing optimism that the country would overcome its current challenges. The monarch made the appeal on Tuesday while speaking with journalists after the installation of the new Kakawa of Lagos, High Chief Jamiu Kakawa, and Eletu of Iwashe, High Chief Teslim Oluwatosin, at his palace in Iga Iduganran, Lagos Island. Akiolu called for cooperation, prayers and trust in God, stressing that unity and understanding among political leaders were essential for national development. He noted that disagreements among politicians were part of the democratic process, warning that political differences should not be mistaken for permanent hostility. According to him, political leaders must be willing to find common ground in the interest of the country. “My special appeal to all Nigerians is to give more time to the incumbent president to complete his assignment. And with the support and prayers of all of us, all will be well,” he said. The monarch added: “All what we require in this country is cooperation, prayer, and closeness to God. “You see my spirit, I’m pleading to all of us in this country that we should give peace a chance. “See the programmes of all these aspirants, see what they have done, and pray for them and support them. All will be well with us, insha Allah.” Akiolu also reiterated his call for Lagos State to be accorded full status, while emphasising the need for mutual respect and cooperation between traditional institutions and government. On the newly enacted State Police Law, the monarch commended the development but urged that its implementation should be guided by fairness and the fear of God. He said the effectiveness of any law depended not only on its enactment but also on how it was enforced and received by the people. “All praise to God Almighty Allah. You know, anybody can make a law, but the application, where you enforce it, and the reaction of the people that matters. “We have been long awaiting the law that we are expecting to come to force. If it is enforced and implemented with the fear of God, everything will be in order,” he said. The event was attended by several dignitaries, including the Chairman of Lagos Island Local Government, Prince Taiwo Oyekan, among others. item.title: We were ignorant to oppose subsidy removal under Jonathan – Chinda
item.description: Rivers State All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, Kingsley Chinda, has admitted that he and other lawmakers were ignorant when they opposed the removal of fuel subsidy during the administration of former President Goodluck Jonathan. Chinda, a member of the House of Representatives, said their opposition was motivated by the belief that they were defending the interests of Nigerians, but they did not understand the economic consequences of retaining the subsidy. He made the remarks at the inauguration of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, where he recalled how lawmakers convened a parliamentary sitting on a Sunday to resist Jonathan’s proposed removal of the subsidy. “We were in a period of ignorance when we stood against fuel subsidy removal. We convened the parliament and sat on a Sunday with Aminu Tambuwal as the Speaker of the House of Representatives. We were all members of the PDP, and the President was PDP,” he said. Chinda explained that lawmakers believed they were acting in the public interest at the time, but later realised that Nigerians had been misled into thinking that fuel subsidy was a benefit they enjoyed without cost. “But because we felt we were speaking for the people, that was why I said it was a period of ignorance. We stood against it. We didn’t know that there were those who were manipulated, those who were doing it for free, and Nigerians who believed that we were enjoying it for free,” he added. The former lawmaker described fuel subsidy as harmful to Nigeria’s economic development, insisting that its removal had increased the revenue available to the federal, state and local governments. “Fuel subsidy is not just a scam. It is against the interests of this country. It is against the development of this country. It is against you and your future,” he said. Chinda also argued that the removal of subsidy had improved government revenue and eased the pressure on public finances, claiming that salary payments at the three tiers of government were no longer the challenge they once were. “Today, all that is history. Salary is no longer a problem, both at the local government, state and federal levels. Why? Because you have more money to the states and more money to the local governments,” he said. “Things are not easy, but for every difficulty you face, just be rest assured that this country is gradually and slowly coming out of the abyss,” he added. Jonathan’s administration faced widespread protests in January 2012 after announcing plans to remove fuel subsidy, triggering the Occupy Nigeria demonstrations across the country. The government eventually reduced the planned increase in petrol prices following the protests. President Bola Tinubu announced the removal of fuel subsidy during his inauguration on May 29, 2023, a decision that led to a sharp increase in petrol prices and heightened cost of living pressures across the country. item.title: Shettima, Makinde seek accountability, national reset
item.description: By Adeola Badru Vice-President Kashim Shettima and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde have called for greater accountability, constructive criticism and a socio-political reset of Nigeria, saying the country must strengthen its democratic institutions and return to the vision of its founding fathers. The two leaders spoke on Tuesday at the public presentation of nine books compiled from the Monday Lines column of Saturday Tribune Editor, Dr Lasisi Olagunju, held at the International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan, Oyo State. The event brought together political leaders, academics, journalists and other dignitaries to celebrate Olagunju’s 15 years of political commentary on Nigeria’s leadership, governance, institutions and national development. Shettima, who delivered his goodwill message virtually, urged Nigerian leaders to embrace constructive criticism, warning that governments that listen only to praise risk losing touch with the people they are elected to serve. He said journalists and intellectuals who challenged those in authority played an important role in strengthening public institutions and deepening democratic accountability. Congratulating Olagunju on the publication of the nine books, the Vice-President described his work as a valuable contribution to Nigerian journalism and intellectual development, adding that preserving the columns in book form would provide future generations with an important record of the country’s political history. “There is a wisdom that says when an elder dies, a library burns. But there is a tragedy we seldom speak about. When a society refuses to listen to its writers, it allows its library to burn while its custodians are still alive,” he said. Describing Olagunju as a journalist who understood the responsibility of the pen in awakening society’s conscience, Shettima said newspapers should serve as more than records of daily events. According to him, “His writings remind us that the newspaper is more than a record of yesterday’s events. It is a conversation between a nation and its conscience.” He said public office holders must resist the temptation to surround themselves with people who only agree with them, noting that criticism could sometimes provide the guidance needed to improve governance. “A government that listens only to praise risks losing touch with the people it was elected to serve,” he said. Shettima, however, stressed that journalists must uphold honesty, fairness and intellectual courage, just as public officials must demonstrate humility, accountability and a willingness to listen. He added that the publication of 15 years of newspaper commentary would preserve the ideas, concerns and debates that shaped a generation. In his remarks, Makinde called for a socio-political reset of Nigeria, arguing that the country must return to the vision of its founding fathers, who adopted federalism to accommodate its diverse nationalities. item.title: Top 10 countries where people spend the most time gaming
item.description: The Philippines has emerged as the country where internet users spend the most time playing video games, with an average of 11 hours and 14 minutes weekly, according to a new global ranking. The ranking, based on research conducted by GWI in the second quarter of 2025 and published in the Digital 2026 Global Overview Report, compares gaming habits across 54 countries and territories. It covers internet users aged 16 and above and includes time spent playing games on mobile phones, computers and gaming consoles. Brazil occupies second position with an average of 10 hours and 56 minutes weekly, while Turkey ranks third with 10 hours and 11 minutes. Mexico and the United States complete the top five, recording 9 hours and 24 minutes and nine hours and nine minutes respectively. The worldwide average stands at six hours and 56 minutes per week, equivalent to just under an hour daily. Five countries in the Americas feature in the top 10, while all five East Asian markets surveyed, including Japan, China and South Korea, rank below the global average. Here are the 10 countries where people spend the most time playing video games. 1. Philippines – 11 hours, 14 minutes The Philippines leads the global ranking, with internet users spending an average of 11 hours and 14 minutes playing video games every week. The figure is the highest among the 54 countries and territories surveyed, placing the Southeast Asian country ahead of major gaming markets worldwide. 2. Brazil – 10 hours, 56 minutes Brazil ranks second, with internet users spending an average of 10 hours and 56 minutes gaming weekly. The South American country is just 18 minutes behind the Philippines, highlighting the popularity of gaming among its internet population. 3. Turkey – 10 hours, 11 minutes Turkey occupies third position, recording an average weekly gaming time of 10 hours and 11 minutes. It is the only country from the Middle East and Europe to feature in the top three. 4. Mexico – 9 hours, 24 minutes Mexico ranks fourth, with internet users spending an average of nine hours and 24 minutes playing video games every week. Its position makes it the second-highest-ranked country from the Americas in the ranking. 5. United States – 9 hours, 9 minutes The United States occupies fifth position, with an average weekly gaming time of nine hours and nine minutes. item.title: Senate approves $20.52bn, €1.045bn borrowing plan
item.description: …Also approves N10.79trn external loan to finance 2026 budget deficit By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Senate has approved President Bola Tinubu’s 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Rolling Plan of $20.517 billion and €1.045 billion, equivalent to about N29.6 trillion. The approval followed the consideration of a report by the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, chaired by Senator Aliyu Wamakko (APC, Sokoto North). The report was presented by the committee’s Vice Chairman, Senator Tokunbo Abiru (APC, Lagos East). The Senate also approved an additional external borrowing request of N10,790,360,835,481 to finance the deficit in the 2026 Appropriation Act. The supplementary borrowing plan comprises $20.517 billion, estimated at N28 trillion, and €1.045 billion, equivalent to approximately N1.6 trillion. The approvals are intended to provide financing for government projects and fiscal commitments under the 2026 and 2027 borrowing programme. The Senate was also asked to approve arrangements to facilitate access to a $7.7 billion external loan component already captured in the 2026 budget. However, the upper chamber clarified that the $7.7 billion facility was an existing budget provision and should not be interpreted as additional borrowing. Under the 2026 fiscal projections presented to the lawmakers, the Federal Government’s revenue is estimated at N33.7 trillion, against projected expenditure of N65.1 trillion, leaving a deficit of N31.4 trillion, representing 5.6 per cent of Gross Domestic Product. Of the planned financing, domestic borrowing is expected to account for N18.4 trillion, representing about 63 per cent, while external borrowing is projected at approximately N10.79 trillion, or 37 per cent. The borrowing component is expected to finance a significant portion of the government’s expenditure requirements. Defending the borrowing proposals, Deputy Senate President, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), dismissed concerns that the facilities would push Nigeria beyond internationally recognised debt sustainability limits. Barau put the country’s debt-to-GDP ratio at about 35 per cent, saying it could rise to 42 per cent following the proposed borrowing, still below the 70 per cent threshold. He also clarified that the $20.517 billion and €1.045 billion facilities would not be accessed immediately, explaining that individual projects and funding requests would be assessed against stipulated requirements and national priorities. “The first request is not something that is going to be drawn down immediately. It is based on requirements. If the requirements are fulfilled, and the requests are in line with our national objectives and priorities, then that will be done on an individual basis,” he said. Barau further explained that the borrowing arrangement accommodated the financing requirements of state governments in addition to those of the Federal Government. item.title: Omo-Agege attack: Doherty condemns violence, demands justice for victims
item.description: The Lagos governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Funso Doherty, has condemned the attack on the campaign activities of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege in Delta State, describing it as a disturbing escalation of political violence. Doherty called for an impartial investigation into the incident and urged security agencies to take immediate steps to protect politicians, supporters and other participants in the electoral process. In a statement following the attack on Monday, he expressed shock over the violence and the reported loss of lives, warning that growing political intolerance, intimidation and bloodshed threatened Nigeria’s democracy. He said no Nigerian should be killed or injured for exercising their constitutional right to support a political party, candidate or express their political views. “My heartfelt condolences go to the families of those who lost loved ones. I wish those injured a speedy and full recovery. There must be no place for political violence in our democracy,” Doherty said. The NDC candidate said political leaders and security agencies had a greater responsibility to protect the country’s democracy amid what he described as a fragile political environment. He called for a thorough investigation into the incident, insisting that those responsible must be identified and prosecuted. “More importantly, immediate steps must be taken to secure participants in our political process and to de-escalate this dangerous trend,” he said. Doherty said political disagreements should be resolved through dialogue, engagement and elections rather than intimidation and violence. He described attacks on political participants as threats to democratic values and nation-building, urging political actors to reject violence. “Employing intimidation and violence is an attack on the very foundation of democracy and must be roundly rejected,” he said. item.title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region. Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State. He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election. According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate. “Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos. “He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said. ﻿ The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour. “And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said. Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections. He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years. “The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said. Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. “And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. item.title: NDC Boycotts IGP’s Meeting Over Alleged Attacks On Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures. The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday. It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country. The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State. It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed. The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State. Omo-Agege is a chieftain of the NDC. Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area. The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh. The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation. However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries. Police Speak The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice. item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. item.title: Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries
item.description: Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures. Ibrahim made the call during deliberations of the UN General Assembly’s Fifth Committee on reports of the United Nations Board of Auditors, where he expressed concern over the number of unresolved audit issues and called for improved performance by the organisation’s management. He acknowledged that 100 audit reports had been cleared but said the 216 outstanding reports remained a significant concern that required urgent attention. Although he recognised that some of the cases might have been overtaken by events, the Nigerian diplomat urged the UN management to improve its clearance rate, which currently stands at 55 per cent. Ibrahim also emphasised the importance of timely payment of assessed contributions by member states, insisting that payments should be made according to schedule and translated into tangible benefits. On financial reporting, he stressed that the accuracy and integrity of data were fundamental to the credibility of reports presented before member states. ﻿ He said all stakeholders had a collective responsibility to safeguard the integrity of information underpinning the UN’s financial reporting. The Nigerian envoy warned that continued explanations without corresponding compliance could leave the organisation trapped in an endless cycle of justifications. He, therefore, urged UN management to prioritise adherence to established financial rules and procedures as the most effective way to address recurring audit concerns. Ibrahim also commended the cooperation between information-gathering systems and audit teams, describing their coordination as essential to improving the quality and reliability of UN reports. Meanwhile, the Fifth Committee considered the Secretary-General’s report on the estimated use of the commitment authority for 2026 and the proposed 2027 subvention to the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia. Speaking on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, Uruguay reaffirmed the group’s support for the proposed subvention, as well as its commitment to justice and national reconciliation. The Committee subsequently concluded its general discussion, with Canada’s representative, Sophia, expected to lead informal consultations to consolidate the observations and contributions of delegations. The Committee is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026. The post Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: NASS Approves Tinubu’s $20.5bn, €1.45bn Supplementary External Borrowing Plan
item.description: The National Assembly has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion for 2026 and 2027. The Senate approved the request on Tuesday following consideration of the recommendations of its Committee on Local and Foreign Loans. The approval came after the House of Representatives also endorsed the President’s borrowing plan. This file photo shows the red chamber of the Nigerian Senate. The proposed borrowing was calculated at an exchange rate of ₦1,400 to the dollar. Earlier on Tuesday, President Tinubu wrote to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the previously approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion. The proposal, titled ‘Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Re-enactment Bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework’, was presented during plenary by Senate President Godswill Akpabio. House of Reps. (Photo by Facebook/House of Representatives, Federal Republic of Nigeria) Akpabio subsequently referred the correspondence to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative consideration. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at ₦65.176 trillion, down from the ₦68.323 trillion earlier approved by the National Assembly. Projected Federal Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion, while capital expenditure is pegged at ₦26.232 trillion. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. Despite the reduction in overall expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at ₦31.457 trillion, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The proposed new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion also remains unchanged. This comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic borrowing and ₦10.790 trillion in external borrowing. Tinubu explained that the proposed $7.7 billion external loan, estimated at ₦10.368 trillion, would finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the overall borrowing limit. According to the President, the adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline. The development comes amid expectations that Tinubu will present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.
